paragraphs: Aircraft mechanics and service technicians (the U.S. counterpart is O*NET/BLS 49-3011 Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians, including A&P mechanics and aviation maintenance technicians, AMT) diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul aircraft engines and components such as hydraulic and pneumatic systems: judge the fault to the maintenance manual, service bulletins and specifications and decide how to repair or replace, use hand tools, measuring instruments and test equipment to inspect and replace worn, defective or damaged parts, inspect the airframe, wings and tail for corrosion, distortion and hidden cracks, test the operation of the engine and the systems, complete the routine and special inspections required by regulation, sign the maintenance release and record all preventive and corrective maintenance. The workplace is the hangar, the apron and the maintenance shop, and the core measures are airworthiness compliance, a re-checkable maintenance record and the release responsibility, not designing aircraft or running an airline. People likely to explore it are usually willing to work precisely within the manual and the authorisation boundary, to verify repeatedly with data and records, and are prepared for the continuing airworthiness responsibility.

An editorially designed paper exercise: use the K-v2 fictional rules below to check six measurement records, keep the inputs and write conforming, non-conforming or evidence pending. The reference answer is A/E conforming, B/C/F non-conforming and D evidence pending; five can be judged and three are non-conforming; the exercise observes only the document version, the criteria and the record check and cannot diagnose a real aircraft or sign a release.

People more likely to adapt: those who can work step by step to the manual and within the authorisation without skipping a step, who are willing to verify repeatedly with measurement data and instruments, who can accept hangar and apron noise, weather and shift pressure and wear the protective equipment as required, and who respect the airworthiness and release responsibility. The risk is usually greater for those unwilling to work to the manual, inclined to skip measurement or recording on experience, or uncomfortable with bearing the release responsibility.

In one sentence: an aviation maintenance post that diagnoses, repairs or overhauls aircraft engines and systems in the hangar, on the apron and in the maintenance shop to the maintenance manual and the continuing airworthiness documents, completes the inspection, testing and maintenance release and leaves a traceable record.

The tasks of aircraft mechanics and service technicians fall into four categories: inspection and fault diagnosis (reading and interpreting the technical material to the maintenance manual, service bulletins and specifications, inspecting the airframe, landing gear, hydraulic and pneumatic systems, de-icing equipment and other components, using precision measuring instruments and test equipment to measure wear and locate cracks, fractures and leaks, and hearing the pilot's description of the fault in order to judge the cause); repair and overhaul (replacing or repairing worn, defective or damaged parts with hand tools, measuring instruments and test equipment, dismantling and reassembling engines and components, reconditioning the airframe structure and the piping, electrical, hydraulic and structural components, and modifying to drawings and engineering instructions); testing and release (testing the operation of the engine and the systems, completing the routine and special inspections required by regulation, inspecting the completed work and certifying that the maintenance meets the standard and the aircraft is operable); and records and coordination (maintaining all preventive and corrective maintenance logs, taking inventory of and requisitioning aviation materials, and coordinating the installation and calibration of heavy components with other trades).

O*NET 49-3011.00 Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians: diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul aircraft engines and components such as hydraulic and pneumatic systems. Common job titles include Aircraft Maintainer, Aircraft Maintenance Technician, Aircraft Mechanic, Airframe and Powerplant Mechanic (A&P), Aviation Maintenance Technician (AMT), aviation mechanic and helicopter mechanic. The work centres on the inspection, repair and release carried out to the maintenance manual and the continuing airworthiness documents.

entries: Inspection and diagnosis｜Manual and criteria｜Read and interpret the maintenance manual, service bulletins and specifications and determine the feasibility and method of repairing or replacing the fault.

Component inspection｜Instruments and non-destructive testing｜Inspect components such as the airframe, landing gear, hydraulic and pneumatic systems, and use precision measuring instruments and X-ray and magnetic inspection equipment to locate wear, corrosion and hidden cracks.

Repair and overhaul｜Dismantling and reconditioning｜Replace or repair worn, defective or damaged parts, dismantle and reassemble engines and recondition the airframe structure and the components of each system.

Testing and inspection｜Operation and regulation｜Test the operation of the engine and the systems, complete the routine and special inspections required by regulation, and certify that the maintenance meets the standard and release it.
Modification and manufacture｜Drawings and tooling｜Modify aircraft structures, systems or components to drawings, engineering instructions and wiring diagrams, and make and fit replacement parts.

Records and coordination｜Logs and aviation materials｜Maintain all preventive and corrective maintenance logs, take inventory of and requisition aviation materials, and coordinate the installation and calibration of heavy components with other trades.

In mainland China CCAR-66-R3 came into force on 2020-07-01: the licence is endorsed by aircraft, rotorcraft and engine category. 66.6 requires being at least 18 years old, no colour blindness or colour weakness affecting maintenance, a college diploma or above, completion of the basic knowledge training, a pass in the licence examination and completion of the aviation maintenance technical English test, and no serious dishonesty record related to maintenance; the experience condition is at least 1 year of authorised maintenance experience with an organisation (excluding training and internship), or a college diploma or above in science or engineering plus the specified practical training. The individual licence remains valid; a complex aircraft additionally requires the corresponding type endorsement. A first application for a type endorsement in a category requires at least 6 consecutive months of internship after the type training examination, and the endorsement is valid for 24 months; the specific maintenance work and release are checked separately against the CCAR-145 organisation project authorisation and personnel conditions.

Maintenance records, inspection and test data, the part and serial numbers of replaced components and the release signature are kept to the Rules on the Certification of Civil Aircraft Maintenance Organisations and the organisation's quality management system, so that a maintenance decision can be traced to the specific work order, data and authorised person.

The boundary rests on four things: who carries out the inspection, repair and release to the manual, who designs and certifies the aircraft, who operates the flights, and who carries out airworthiness oversight. Aircraft mechanics and service technicians carry out the inspection and repair and sign the release to the continuing airworthiness documents within the authorisation and the type; the design and airworthiness certification of the aircraft and systems are the responsibility of the design organisation and the certification authority; flight operations and dispatch are the responsibility of the operator; airworthiness and operational oversight are the responsibility of the Civil Aviation Administration of China and its regional administrations; anything beyond the authorisation or the type limitation must be escalated to the organisation's procedure.
Carry out the inspection and repair and sign the maintenance release to the continuing airworthiness documents within the authorisation and the type.

The object is the aircraft airframe, engines, propellers and onboard systems and components; the basis is the maintenance manual, the service bulletins, the airworthiness directives, the continuing airworthiness documents and the organisation's maintenance procedure.

Aircraft mechanics and service technicians (the U.S. counterpart is O*NET/BLS 49-3011 Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians, including airframe and powerplant mechanics, A&P, and aviation maintenance technicians, AMT) diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul aircraft engines and components: inspect and judge the fault to the maintenance manual and the service bulletins, use precision measuring instruments and test equipment to inspect parts for wear, corrosion and cracks, replace or repair defective parts, test the operation of the systems and complete the routine and special inspections required by regulation, sign the maintenance release and record all maintenance activity. The workplace is the hangar, the apron and the maintenance shop. On the mainland China side, the maintenance personnel licence, the type endorsement and the maintenance release follow the Rules on the Administration of Licences for Civil Aircraft Maintenance Personnel (CCAR-66-R3), and the maintenance organisation and quality management follow the Rules on the Certification of Civil Aircraft Maintenance Organisations (CCAR-145). In boundary terms it is not the same as an aircraft design and airworthiness certification post, nor the same as a flight operations and dispatch post.

Measurement data and inspection results can assist the judgement, but determining the repair method to the manual, certifying that the maintenance meets the standard and signing the release are still borne by authorised maintenance personnel.

Work is divided by aircraft type and specialism, and before starting you should check the employer's authorisation scope, type endorsement and quality management requirements.

Maintenance work and independent release must be checked separately: a supervised or organisation-authorised maintenance post does not necessarily hold the release authority; an independent release additionally requires the certificate, type and specific project authorisation of the jurisdiction concerned. Design certification, operational dispatch and airworthiness oversight remain other duties.
The licence category and type endorsement and the organisation authorisation and quality management procedure are set out in the regulations and the organisation manual.

A complex aircraft may be released only after obtaining the corresponding type endorsement; maintenance or release must not exceed the licence category, the type limitation or the organisation authorisation; the licence privileges must not be exercised when the physical condition is unsuitable (for example intoxication or illness); and a defect or an unairworthy condition found must be reported promptly as required.

A defect, an out-of-tolerance condition or an unairworthy condition found must be reported as required and the record kept, and must not be concealed because of flight pressure nor released for maintenance that does not meet the standard.

A maintenance and release record applies only to the corresponding aircraft, type and piece of work; a single inspection conclusion must not be extrapolated to another type or to a long-term state, and a system prompt must not be treated as the basis for a release.

Before starting, check at least six things: the employer type (airline, independent maintenance organisation, aircraft manufacturer or component repair company); the specialist direction (line maintenance, base check and overhaul, or engine and component overhaul); the aircraft type and authorisation (whether an A&P licence or an organisation type authorisation is needed and which types are involved); the licence and training pathway (the conditions and duration for the U.S. A&P or the Chinese CCAR-66-R3 licence); the shift and environment (shift work, night work, hangar and apron exposure, protective equipment); and the training investment and promotion path.
Look at the employer type and the specialist direction, not at the job title.

Employer type: an airline's engineering department, an independent maintenance organisation (MRO), an aircraft manufacturer or a component repair company; different employers have different authorisation systems and business tempos.
The specialist direction determines the daily tasks and the skill emphasis.

Specialist direction: line maintenance (transit and fault rectification), base check and overhaul (structural repair and system inspection) or engine and component overhaul (dismantling, inspection and test running).
The aircraft type and the authorisation determine the scope of work that may be carried out.

Aircraft type and authorisation: whether an A&P licence (United States) or an aircraft maintenance personnel licence and type endorsement (China) is needed, and which aircraft types and engine categories are involved.
The licence, the training and the post authorisation must be checked against the jurisdiction and the specific duties, and an assistant or supervised post differs from an independent release.

A U.S. FAA certificate may cover airframe A, powerplant P or both; a single rating requires at least 18 months of experience and both together at least 30 months, or an approved school and other alternative route, with examination and English requirements, and no uniform prior education condition. A Chinese licence application is checked against Article 66.6 of CCAR-66-R3 for a college diploma or above, basic training, authorised maintenance experience or science and engineering practical training and the other conditions.
The working environment places continuous demands on physical effort and health.

Shift and environment: whether there is shift and night work, noise and temperature exposure in the hangar and on the apron, work in cramped spaces and at height, and the protective equipment and occupational health arrangements.
The authorisation scope and the promotion path affect long-term earnings and development.

Authorisation and promotion: whether more type endorsements and release authorisations can be obtained, whether a move into engineering support, quality management or training is possible, and the promotion path.

Four classes of risk need the earliest judgement: first, the maintenance and airworthiness risk (skipping a manual criterion or an inspection step, or failing to record or sign the release as required); second, the authorisation risk (working beyond the licence category, the type endorsement or the organisation authorisation); third, the safety and health risk (work at height and in cramped spaces, high-pressure hydraulic and electrical work, test-running noise and contaminant exposure, shift fatigue); and fourth, the material risk (using an out-of-date or inapplicable manual or engineering material). The risk varies with the specialist direction: line maintenance is closer to time pressure and rapid judgement, base check and overhaul to process steps and structural repair, and engine and component overhaul to precision measurement and assembly tolerances.

Evidence scope: O*NET 49-3011.00 provides the tasks and the work context (76% exposed to distracting noise every day, 77% considering precision or accuracy extremely important, 42% in contact with hazardous conditions every day and 24% in cramped space or awkward positions every day); the BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics provides the wages and employment; the Rules on the Administration of Licences for Civil Aircraft Maintenance Personnel (CCAR-66-R3) provide the framework requirements for the mainland China licence, type endorsement and release authority. values: The exercise-defined rules and the six original records

K-v2 is an editorially fictional rule: the object is only the T test piece and the figures have no unit and are not aircraft parameters; every row must have a number, an object, a revision and a reading. Only when the object is T, the revision is K-v2 and the reading is within the closed interval 10.0 to 12.0 may the row be marked 'conforming in this exercise'. The six original records: A｜T｜K-v2｜10.0; B｜T｜K-v2｜12.1; C｜T｜K-v1｜11.0; D｜T｜K-v2｜reading missing; E｜T｜K-v2｜12.0; F｜U｜K-v2｜11.0.

Non-conformance and a missing item are kept separate: a clearly different revision or object, or a reading outside the interval, is non-conforming; a missing reading is evidence pending. The original record must not be guessed at or overwritten.
Hand in the six-row result, the reason for each row, the conforming/non-conforming/pending counts and a summary that discusses only the record check; do not use a real aircraft or maintenance manual.
Reference answer and counts

Cover this answer sheet while answering independently. Reference answer: A conforms, at the lower bound; B is non-conforming (12.1 is greater than 12.0); C is non-conforming (old revision); D is evidence pending (reading missing); E conforms, at the upper bound; F is non-conforming (different object).
Independent totals: conforming 2, non-conforming 3 and evidence pending 1, with 2+3+1=6; of the five judgeable records 3 are non-conforming, that is 3/5=60%, which is not a failure rate.
Summary, observation sheet and independent recheck

Example summary: 'Six K-v2 paper records; A/E conform; B/C/F are non-conforming; D has a missing reading, so the original record is kept and evidence is pending. The real equipment state or repair method cannot be determined.' The scoring is an editorial observation sheet: 1 point for each of the six-row results, 1 point for the specific reason for each row, 1 point for the three correct totals, 1 point for the 3/5 ratio and the denominator explanation, and 1 point for not altering a missing item and stating the real authority boundary, 15 points in total.

This exercise observes document applicability, threshold comparison, record completeness and handover expression and cannot confirm real aviation maintenance capability. entries.answer: Diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul aircraft engines and components to the maintenance manual, the service bulletins and the specifications: inspect parts such as the fuselage, the landing gear and the hydraulic and pneumatic systems; use precision measuring instruments and non-destructive testing equipment to locate wear, corrosion and cracks; replace or repair defective components; remove and install engines; test the operation of the systems; complete the routine and special inspections required by regulation; keep the maintenance log; and sign the maintenance release as required.
entries.question: What does an aircraft mechanic and service technician do each day?

entries.answer: This occupation focuses on the inspection, maintenance and recording of aircraft in service; design engineering, operations and regulation have separate duties. The avionics post leans more towards airborne electronics and instruments, but a mechanic may also repair electrical components, so the knowledge and authority overlap and must be checked against the specific jurisdiction and employer.
entries.question: Where is the boundary between this occupation and adjacent posts?

entries.answer: The current sources are insufficient to estimate this occupation's AI substitution rate, job reduction or disappearance year. The BLS2025—2035 projection of 5.4% growth and about 11,400 average annual openings for this occupation is a combined employment projection and cannot be interpreted as caused by AI or as proof that AI will not replace it.

entries.answer: Mainland China has no precise national wage distribution for this occupation; this page gives only a broad reference from the National Bureau of Statistics for 2025, by industry category and unit type (for example, 133,981 yuan a year for non-private units in transport, storage and postal services, and 113,594 yuan a year for non-private manufacturing), and these figures cover a great many non-maintenance posts and cannot be taken as this occupation's wage.

entries.answer: U.S. definition: in 2025, month 5 (May), 49-3011 had a median annual wage of 79,870 U.S. dollars (an hourly wage of 38.40 U.S. dollars), with the 10th percentile at 48,780 U.S. dollars, the 25th percentile at 62,630 U.S. dollars, the 75th percentile at 99,130 U.S. dollars and the 90th percentile at 128,890 U.S. dollars (BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics OEWS, displayed through O*NET). A percentile is a position in a statistical distribution and does not represent a starting wage.
entries.question: What is the wage for this occupation in the United States?

entries.answer: On entry, first separate the jurisdiction and the duties: a U.S. FAA certificate A/P may be for one or both ratings, the training or experience and the examination must be checked officially, and there is no uniform prior education condition; unlicensed assistance work is limited to statutory supervision or the organisation authority. China's CCAR-66-R3 governs the individual licence and the type endorsement, and Article 145.21 of CCAR-145R4 distinguishes the maintenance personnel project authorisation from the release person's licence, experience and release project authorisation; a domestic aircraft release person has at least two years of relevant maintenance experience. A learning deliverable cannot replace any of those authorisations.
entries.question: How can someone become a maintenance worker in this occupation?

entries.answer: Mainly skipping a manual criterion or an inspection step, failing to record or sign the release as required, working outside the type and authorisation scope, hazardous work and insufficient protection (work at height and in confined spaces, hydraulics and electrical systems, test-run noise and contaminants), using out-of-date or inapplicable documents, and shift fatigue. Following the manual step by step, recording truthfully, signing the release only for maintenance that meets the standard and taking recurrent training as required are the basic controls; the specific provisions follow the competent authority and the organisation's quality management system.
entries.question: What are the main risks of this occupation?

entries.answer: The latest BLS 2025—2035 projection: 49-3011 with 140,000 people in the base year, a rise of 5.4% and average annual openings of about 11,400. The OOH shows this occupation's growth rounded to 5%, and the 6% and 13,100 openings that combine the mechanic and avionics occupations cannot be substituted. Openings are not net new posts or a guarantee of hiring, and cannot be extrapolated to China.
entries.question: What is the employment outlook in the United States?

entries.answer: Work in hangars, on the apron and in maintenance workshops: 76% are exposed to distracting noise every day, 72% work indoors in a non-environmentally-controlled setting every day, 33% work outdoors and are exposed to all kinds of weather every day, 77% consider precision or accuracy extremely important, 42% are exposed to hazardous conditions every day, and 24% are in a confined space or an awkward posture every day; shifts and night work are common (O*NET 49-3011.00 respondent shares).
entries.question: What is the work environment like?

entries.answer: Start with the work object and the preference (quick judgement under operational pressure / check work steps and structural repair / precision measurement and assembly tolerances), then look at the licence category and the type endorsement, and finally confirm the employer type, the shift and the environment. The three directions share the ability to interpret documents to the manual, to measure precisely, to judge a fault and to record the release, but the focus of the specialised training and the type of risk differ.
